findings.finding: P is introduced as a plant mousse and D as a dairy dessert without expressly assigning either the non-heat-treated state required by the cited rows. The assumption about ingredients belonging to the matching additive groups does not establish the products heat-treatment status. Consequently the presently unconditional reference decisions ask learners to import a legally decisive fact.
findings.evidence: The dated PDF rows313/314 expressly restrict both cases by heat-treatment status; neutral M8 states those restrictions for the rules but does not state that property for P or D themselves.
findings.minimalCorrection: In DE and EN explicitly define P as a non-heat-treated plant-based mousse and D as a non-heat-treated dairy-based dessert before the tasks. Keep the combined group/free-acid assumptions. Alternatively leave the fact open and accept conditional or insufficient-information answers, but the short explicit example clarification is the smaller repair.
findings.reasonForRevision: The task specifically examines correct categories and source limits; a learner who notices the missing product fact must not be marked wrong for withholding an unconditional legal-table comparison.

taskByTask.reason: Lower pH increases undissociated acid at the same pKa. Relating the bounded membrane model and supplied counts while naming matrix, amount or organism limits is chemically sound; no causal universal claim from unmatched A/B data is required.
Electron donation and oxidation of ascorbic acid coupled to reagent reduction are distinct from microbial inhibition. Supplied C counts support only the stated bounded conclusion.
Equal10mL aliquots and the expressly selective proportional method give3.2/4.0=0.80 and0.40g/L. Method/selectivity limits and units are properly assessed.

A is supported within supplied microbial-count/ascorbate data. Missing additive quantities, starting/time-series vitamin levels, food-law status and safety evidence explicitly prevent stronger claims.

Drying/salting versus controlled pasteurisation/cooling is an appropriate historical/current comparison. Water availability, vegetative-cell reduction, non-sterility, recontamination and cold-chain risks are sound; the learner must justify a food-specific combination.

Actual viewed A is butanoic acid and B ethyl ethanoate, eachC4H8O2. Recognition ofCOOH, correct full structures, methanoic-to-butanoic homologous series and acid-indicator/hydrogencarbonate observations jointly cover the stated carboxylic-acid components. Acidic observations alone are correctly not treated as unique structural identification. This is supplied-evidence interpretation, no claim of own laboratory execution.

Conjugate pairs, O-H polarity and two acetate contributors with total charge-1 are correct; ethoxide lacks that carboxylate delocalisation. The provided pKa values support chloroacetic>3-chloropropanoic>ethanoic acid, explained qualitatively by distance-dependent-I. No mesomerism through saturatedCH2 or alternating isolated contributors is asserted.
Correct free-acid conversion direction and pH interpretation; repair F1 product precondition and F2 rounding. Once P is explicitly non-heat-treated,523.93>500 is the correct bounded table conclusion.
350>300 is numerically correct only after making D explicitly non-heat-treated. Separation of the plant case, restricted juice exception and present-day source checks is otherwise correct.

This is compatible with dropwise addition, not a claimed successful run or measured endpoint. A uses only0.2mg DCPIP in1mL, also compatible with a small positive-control addition.

taskByTask.reason: A genuinely locally checked complete plan is required before execution; this AI review neither supplies nor certifies that release.
Learner must actually execute DCPIP A with immediate raw blank/positive/unknown data. Supplied observations or simulation cannot score execution.
Fresh iodine/starch B plus another reducing comparator gives a real own variation and interference check, provided the local plan selects the reagent and the work actually occurs.

Control validity and honest repeats take priority over forced positive identity. Neutral oxidised DCPIP is blue; valid decolourisation is compatible with reduction, while pH/sample colour or failed controls limit the inference.
Coupled electron donation/oxidation of ascorbate and acceptance/reduction by the reagent explain the antioxidant model without equating pH colour with redox.

C6H8O6 -> C6H6O6 +2H+ +2e- and I2 +2e- ->2I- sum to the provided equation. C,H,O,I and net charge0 are balanced. In KI medium molecular-iodine equivalents are a valid redox bookkeeping form; iodide complexation does not alter the two-electron stoichiometry.
Own interference results, pH/matrix controls, lack of quantitative calibration and explicit limits on health/microbial/product claims correctly bound a qualitative reducing-agent test.
